He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall Pirates]]. Mamukelashvili attended [[Montverde Academy]] after a stint on a youth team in Biella, Italy. As a junior at Seton Hall, Mamukelashvili missed several weeks with a wrist injury but averaged 11.9 points per game. He was named [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East co-Player of the Year]] as a senior. ==Early life== Mamukelashvili was born in New York City and grew up in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] after his family moved to Tbilisi when he was a baby. He is fluent in English, Georgian, Russian, and Italian. His grandmother, Ira Gabashvili, was a member of the [[Soviet Union women's national basketball team|Soviet women's national basketball team]]. Mamukelashvili's older brother David introduced him to basketball at a young age, and Sandro grew up idolizing the Georgian player [[Zaza Pachulia]].{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Seton Hall has a player with a 'big' NBA future (and it's not Myles Powell) |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2019/12/seton-hall-has-a-player-with-a-big-nba-future-and-its-not-myles-powell.html |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=December 4, 2019}} David currently teaches English and philosophy at [[Newark Academy]] in Livingston, New Jersey.{{cite web | url=https://www.newarka.edu/about/faculty-and-staff-directory?2493883_contentId=2493883&2493883_deptId=29103&2493883_gId=&2493883_letter= | title=Faculty & Staff Directory | Newark Academy }} He was in Chicago visiting his aunt, pianist [[Eteri Andjaparidze]], when the [[Russo-Georgian War]] broke out in August 2008.{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Gary |title=A world away from war, Sandro Mamukelashvili has found a home at Seton Hall |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/154358/2017/11/14/a-world-away-from-war-sandro-mamukelashvili-has-found-a-home-at-seton-hall/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=November 14, 2017}} When he was 14 years old, Mamukelashvili moved to [[Biella]], Italy to attend high school. He competed on the U17, U18, and U19 teams, and he helped the teams to finish third place in the national finals. Mamukelashvili said that moving to Italy was difficult but his club and head coach Federico Danna made everything possible for him. In 2016, he moved to the United States to attend [[Montverde Academy]], where he played alongside [[Toronto Raptors]] player [[RJ Barrett]]. While at Montverde, Pachulia became a mentor to Mamukelashvili and introduced him to several players such as [[Stephen Curry]]. Mamukelashvili scored 11 points in a 72–45 win over [[Greensboro Day School]] to help Montverde reach the finals of the [[Dick's Sporting Goods]] High School Nationals.{{cite news |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=Third-seeded Montverde earns a trip back to DICK'S title game |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/third-seeded-montverde-earns-a-trip-back-to-dicks-title-game |access-date=April 17, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=March 31, 2017}} On April 20, 2017, Mamukelashvili committed to playing college basketball for [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] over offers from [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]]. He chose the Pirates because his high school coach Kevin Boyle had a good relationship with Seton Hall coach [[Kevin Willard]] and his brother David lived nearby.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Seton Hall freshman adds new dimension, 'will play significant minutes' |url=https://nypost.com/2017/10/31/seton-hall-freshman-adds-new-dimension-will-play-significant-minutes/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=October 31, 2017}} ==College career== [[File:Sandro Mamukelashvili.jpg|thumb|207x207px|Mamukelashvili with [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] in 2019]] As a freshman, Mamukelashvili averaged 2.6 points, 1.9 rebounds and 0.5 blocks per game and helped the Pirates reach the second round of the NCAA Tournament. His best game as a freshman came against [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] on February 14, 2018, when he scored 17 points and grabbed seven rebounds. As a sophomore, he averaged 8.9 points and 7.8 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Seton Hall basketball: Mamukelashvili 'coming out with an edge' |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2019/09/27/seton-hall-basketball-sandro-mamukelashvili/3772961002/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[Asbury Park Press]] |date=September 27, 2019}} On December 19, Mamukelashvili scored a season-high 23 points on 8-of-11 shooting and had eight rebounds in a 90–76 win over [[Sacred Heart Pioneers men's basketball|Sacred Heart]].{{cite news |title=Seton Hall storms past Sacred Heart for fourth straight win |url=https://nypost.com/2018/12/19/seton-hall-storms-past-sacred-heart-for-fourth-straight-win/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 19, 2018}} Following his sophomore season, Mamukelashvili worked with Pachulia at his Academy in Tbilisi to expand his game, adding a jump stop and improving his three-point shooting. On November 29, 2019, Mamukelashvili scored 18 points on 7-of-10 shooting and had six rebounds in an 84–76 win over [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] in the Bahamas. During the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] tournament, Mamukelashvili averaged 14 points, 5.7 rebounds and 2 assists per game while making 61 percent of his shots from the field and 60 percent from behind the arc. He fractured his right wrist in a game against Iowa State on December 8 and missed several weeks.{{cite news |title=Seton Hall loses Sandro Mamukelashvili for up to 2 months |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28268980/seton-hall-loses-sandro-mamukelashvili-2-months |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 10, 2019}} On January 29, 2020, he returned to the court, playing five minutes in a 64–57 win over [[2019–20 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]].{{cite news |last1=Fonseca |first1=Brian |title=Why Seton Hall's Kevin Willard was encouraged by Sandro Mamukelashvili's short return vs. DePaul |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2020/01/why-seton-halls-kevin-willard-was-encouraged-by-sandro-mamukelashvilis-short-return-vs-depaul.html |access-date=February 4, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=January 30, 2020}} On February 19, with his father Zurab in attendance for the first time in two years, Mamukelashvili scored 15 points and had six rebounds, hitting the game-winning shot on an inbounds pass with 0.6 seconds remaining in a 74–72 win over [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].{{cite news |last1=Kussoy |first1=Howie |title=Sandro Mamukelashvili buzzer-beater gives Seton Hall thrilling win |url=https://nypost.com/2020/02/19/sandro-mamukelashvili-buzzer-beater-gives-seton-hall-thrilling-win/ |access-date=February 20, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=February 19, 2020}} He had a season-high 26 points on February 29, in an 88–79 win over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite news |title=Powell leads No. 13 Seton Hall past Marquette 88–79 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168421 |access-date=March 4, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 29, 2020}} Mamukelashvili averaged 11.9 points and 6 rebounds per game as a junior. After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an [[Sports agent|agent]], signaling high potential to return to Seton Hall for his senior campaign.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Seton Hall's Sandro Mamukelashvili to test NBA Draft waters |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2020/03/seton-halls-sandro-mamukelashvili-to-test-nba-draft-waters.html |access-date=March 21, 2020 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=March 20, 2020}} After receiving second round interest, Mamukelashvili announced on August 1 that he was withdrawing from the draft and returning for his senior season.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Sandro Mamukelashvili returning to Seton Hall after NBA draft interest |url=https://nypost.com/2020/08/01/sandro-mamukelashvili-returning-to-seton-hall-after-nba-draft-interest/ |access-date=August 2, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=August 1, 2020}} Coming into his senior season, Mamukelashvili was named to the Preseason First Team All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]], and he was expected to help replace the graduated [[Myles Powell]].{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Seton Hall's emerging star is ready to step up with Myles Powell gone |url=https://nypost.com/2020/10/29/sandro-mamukelashvili-is-ready-to-step-up-for-seton-hall/ |access-date=October 31, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=October 29, 2020}} On December 11, 2020, he scored a career-high 32 points and had nine rebounds and three assists in a 77–68 victory against [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]].{{cite news |last1=O'Brien |first1=Owen |title=St. John's can't handle Sandro Mamukelashvili in loss to Seton Hall |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/st-johns/red-storm-st-john-s-georgetown-chris-mullin-patrick-ewing-a33262 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803154640/https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/st-johns/red-storm-st-john-s-seton-hall-1.50089340 |url-status=live |archive-date=August 3, 2021 |access-date=August 3, 2021 |work=[[Newsday]] |date=December 11, 2020}} On February 16, 2021, Mamukelashvili scored his 1,000th career point in a 60–52 win against [[2020–21 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|DePaul]] and finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and four assists.{{cite news |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Seton Hall basketball survives DePaul as Mamukelashvili dominates, scores 1,000th point |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2021/02/17/seton-hall-depaul-basketball/6778364002/ |access-date=August 3, 2021 |work=[[Asbury Park Press]] |date=February 17, 2021}} He averaged 17.5 points, 7.6 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game. At the close of the season, he was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East co-Player of the Year]] (alongside [[Collin Gillespie]] and [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]]){{cite news |title=Mamukelashvili, Robinson-Earl, Gillespie Share BIG EAST Player of the Year |url=https://www.bigeast.com/news/2021/3/10/mens-basketball-mamukelashvili-robinson-earl-gillespie-share-big-east-player-of-the-year.aspx |access-date=19 January 2026 |work=www.bigeast.com |date=10 March 2021 |language=en}} and won the [[Haggerty Award]] as the best player in the New York metropolitan area. Mamukelashvili was also named Associated Press All-America honorable mention and was a finalist for the [[Karl Malone Award]].{{cite news|url=https://shupirates.com/news/2021/4/27/mens-basketball-sandro-mamukelashvili-wins-2021-haggerty-met-player-of-the-year-award.aspx|title=Sandro Mamukelashvili Wins 2021 Haggerty Met Player of the Year Award|publisher=[[Seton Hall Pirates]]|date=April 27, 2021|access-date=April 27, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2021–2023)=== Mamukelashvili was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 54th pick by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. He was then traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] along with the draft rights of [[Georgios Kalaitzakis]], the 60th pick, and two future second round picks in exchange for the draft rights of the 31st pick, [[Isaiah Todd]].{{cite news|first=Jerry|last=Carino|title=What to know about Milwaukee Bucks draft pick and Seton Hall grad Sandro Mamukelashvili|url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/nba/2021/07/28/nba-draft-seton-hall-sandro-mamukelashvili-steal/5397909001/|work=[[Asbury Park Press]]|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} On August 4, 2021, the Bucks signed him to a [[two-way contract]]. Under the terms of the deal he would split time between the Bucks and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Sandro Mamukelashvili To A Two-way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-sandro-mamukelashvili-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021}} On October 19, 2021, Mamukelashvili had his debut in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], coming off the bench with an assist and a rebound in a 127–104 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Bucks begin title defense with 127-104 victory over Nets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401358773|date=October 19, 2021|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 19, 2021}} On October 26, he was assigned to the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite news |last1=Radcliffe |first1=JR |title=How does the G League work for the Milwaukee Bucks and Wisconsin Herd? |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2021/10/26/how-does-g-league-work-milwaukee-bucks-wisconsin-herd/8556275002/ |access-date=October 28, 2021 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |date=October 26, 2021}} On November 29, while playing with the Herd, Mamukelashvili posted 28 points, six rebounds, three assists, three blocks, and one steal in a win against the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite news |title=Bucks' Sandro Mamukelashvili: Posts 28 points in G League return |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-sandro-mamukelashvili-posts-28-points-in-g-league-return/ |access-date=December 29, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 1, 2021}} He missed two games with an illness in December 2021.{{cite news |title=Bucks' Sandro Mamukelashvili: Off injury report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-sandro-mamukelashvili-off-injury-report/ |access-date=December 29, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 24, 2021}} Mamukelashvili joined the Bucks' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster. On July 18, 2022, Mamukelashvili was named to the All-NBA Summer League First Team.{{cite web | last=Zagoria | first=Adam | title=NBA Summer League: Ex-Seton Hall star Sandro Mamukelashvili named to All-NBA Summer League team | website=NJ.com | date=2022-07-18 | url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2022/07/nba-summer-league-ex-seton-hall-star-sandro-mamukelashvili-named-to-all-nba-summer-league-team.html | access-date=2025-12-09}} On March 1, 2023, Mamukelashvili was waived by the Bucks.{{Cite web |date=March 1, 2023 |title=Milwaukee Bucks Request Waivers on Sandro Mamukelashvili |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-request-waivers-on-sandro-mamukelashvili |access-date=March 1, 2023 |website=NBA}} === San Antonio Spurs (2023–2025) === On March 3, 2023, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] claimed Mamukelashvili off of waivers and converted his deal to a standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Tom Orsborn on Twitter: "Spurs announce they have claimed F Sandro Mamukelashvili off waivers and converted his deal to a standard NBA contract. In addition, they've waived F Isaiah Roby. The roster stands at 17 players."|url=https://twitter.com/tom_orsborn/status/1631785119693299714|website=Twitter.com|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=March 3, 2023}} On July 27, he re-signed with the Spurs.{{cite web|author=saspshirley|title=Spurs Re-Sign Sandro Mamukelashvili|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-sandro-mamukelashvili|website=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2023|access-date=July 27, 2023}} On July 22, 2024, Mamukelashvili re-signed with the Spurs.{{cite web|author=saspshirley|title=Spurs Re-Sign Sandro Mamukelashvili|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-sandro-mamukelashvili-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2023}} On March 19, 2025, Mamukelashvili scored a career-high 34 points with nine rebounds, three assists and a steal in 19 minutes of action off the bench in a 120–105 win over the [[New York Knicks]]. This also broke the record for the most points in a game playing less than 20 minutes.{{cite web |date=March 19, 2025 |title=Mamukelashvili's career-high 34 points, 7 3-pointers fuel Spurs past Knicks 120-105 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705569 |access-date=March 19, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} === Toronto Raptors (2025–2026) === On July 4, 2025, Mamukelashvili signed a two-year, $5.5 million contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |title=RAPTORS SIGN MAMUKELASHVILI|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-mamukelashvili|date=July 4, 2025|work=NBA.com}} He played a [[sixth man]] role for the team, appearing in 80 games for an average 21.9 minutes in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]].{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-06-29 |title=Report: Raptors' Sandro Mamukelashvili declines $2.8-million player option |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/report-raptors-sandro-mamukelashvili-declines-2-8-million-player-option/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |language=en}} Mamukelashvili averaged 11.2 points per game on 52.3% field goal shooting, both career-highs,{{Cite web |last=Pavon |first=Josue |date=2026-05-05 |title=Key Raptors backup sounds off on future after Cavs series loss |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/key-raptors-backup-sounds-off-012017489.html |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |language=en-US |agency=[[ClutchPoints]]}} along with 38.9% shooting from three-point range, 4.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. He saw his first playoff appearance with the Raptors in their first round series defeat to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], averaging five points, five rebounds and one assist across seven games. On June 29, 2026, Mamukelashvili declined his $2.8 million player option for the 2026–27 season, making him a free agent.{{Cite web |title=Sandro Mamukelashvili: Declines player option |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/sandro-mamukelashvili-declines-player-option/ |access-date=July 7, 2026 |website=CBS Sports}} === Los Angeles Lakers (2026–present) === On July 7, 2026, Mamukelashvili signed a four-year, $52 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Forward Sandro Mamukelashvili |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-forward-sandro-mamukelashvili |website=July 7, 2026 |publisher=[[Los Angeles Lakers]]}} ==National team career== In July 2018, Mamukelashvili
